Byte capture inventory

Summary: read-only syntax scan of current Python and shell helpers under scripts/. Every displayed file uses an opaque code. The code-to-path table and source digests remain in a separate local file; no source text or paths are emitted here.

Revision history

RevisionDateChange and reason
A2026-10-22Record capture candidates and reviewed byte paths to prevent newline conversion during repairs.

Method and limits

AST inspection includes text, universal_newlines, encoding and errors options, subprocess aliases, injected runners, dynamic keyword options and explicit/default decode calls. Shell inspection includes substitutions, legacy backticks and embedded Python candidates. Write indicators are conservative: logging and generated outputs can appear as rewrites; read-only candidates can call indirect writers. Decode calls may consume files rather than subprocesses. NOT_EVALUATED means that a byte contract and capture-to-write data flow have not been established; it does not mean safe.

Non-regular paths, including symbolic links, are recorded without following them. Syntax errors remain visible as NOT_EVALUATED. Detection cannot resolve arbitrary wrappers, constructed shell commands, sourced helpers or runtime option dictionaries.

Reviewed contracts and exclusions are recorded in BYTE_PRESERVING and REVIEWED_OTHER. The pointer repair already captures its content as bytes; its subprocess text calls read metadata. The bootstrap writer writes original member bytes after validation. No content subprocess change is required in either reviewed utility. Other candidates require manual triage before claiming audit closure. No shared Git helper is introduced: fewer than three reviewed utilities need a content-capture fix. Existing snapshot relabelling is outside scope.

Regenerate with scripts/quality/byte_capture_audit.py, supplying --report and --local-map destinations explicitly. The mapping destination must be outside the repository. Codes can change on regeneration; retain the paired map for lookup.

Sources

  • Python 3.11 subprocess: newline conversion in text mode
  • Python 3.11 open: newline and surrogateescape
  • Python 3.11 codecs: BOM bytes and signature handling
  • Git show: plain blob contents
  • Git ls-files: NUL-separated filenames
  • Git hash-object: disposable blob fixtures
  • Git init: isolated test repositories
  • Bash: trailing newline removal
